claims.text: Controlled, low-thermal-load selective laser sintering can mitigate residual thermal stresses in AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
Controlled, low-thermal-load selective laser sintering can improve the mechanical properties of AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
The proposed intervention is applicable to AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock.
The applicable processing window combines low thermal load with optimized laser power and scanning speed.
The SLS intervention affects densification and microstructure formation.
Low-thermal-load SLS reduces thermal gradients relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
SLS-processed components will have improved mechanical properties relative to components made under conventional high-thermal-load additive-manufacturing conditions.
SLS-processed components will have lower residual stresses than components made under conventional high-thermal-load additive-manufacturing conditions.
The proposed process will be simpler than conventional high-thermal-load additive-manufacturing regimes.
The hypothesis is limited to miniature component geometries with dimensions below 10 mm.
Optimal SLS parameters for AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock are not established by the supplied information.
